methodology: Forty fresh paired calibration replicates on the original4096 worlds and seven frozen policies. Selection240 is independent of the120/240/480/960 certification looks. Reuse exact registered tests and conservative23-contrast bounded Hoeffding paired intervals. The sole primary contrast is all-policy union requests saved by refusal against early acceptance. Repeats and all policy input evaluations count. Comparator labels and post-decision census work are evaluator costs.
methodology_note: Logical equality and inclusion are pathwise controls. The unchanged finite test family supplies per-replicate error<=.01 under stationary iid sampling; forty replicates do not establish rare-event guarantees. Census safety and label benefit are separate. Oracle truth cannot establish independent natural-language generalization. Deterministic oracle computation reuses labels already requested during selection or certification. Every ordinal fetch, including cache hits, is paid. Full wall time is descriptive, with no speed benefit claim.

protocol.census_scope: evaluator only; after all service decisions
protocol.family_error: 84/16800+28/5600=.01 per replicate; unchanged tests; forty replicates do not prove a rare-event bound

interval_contract.coverage_gate: pathwise inclusion proof, not descriptive interval

alpha_allocation.scope: per replicate conditional on frozen selection

methods.bound_proof: Condition on frozen policies, population and independent selection. Accepted errors conditional on accepted n are binomial at the fixed group risk. Each exact one-sided bound undercovers with probability at most its alpha; n=0 refuses. Union bound over 84 early events and 28 distinct shared final events is .005+.005=.01. Stopping only selects events in this family. Shared or dependent policy tests need no independence. This is a per-replicate guarantee, not a guarantee across all forty replicates or nonstationary draws. This is a new local construction, not the cited paper theorem.
methods.coverage_inclusion_proof: For every possible candidate sequence and frozen selected cutoff, let F be the common final test and E1,E2,E3 the early tests. Fixed certifies iff F. Sequential certifies iff E1 or E2 or E3 or F. Therefore F implies sequential certification, even when sequential stopped earlier. The certified frozen policy serves the same input-only accepted set, so fixed served sets are subsets of sequential served sets in every group and every nonnegative mixture. This logical inclusion requires no probabilistic assumption and says nothing about correctness of answers. Risk validity separately requires iid stationary within-group draws independent of selection and policies.

interval_contract.coverage_gate: pathwise inclusion proof, not descriptive interval

methods.label_cost_definition: Standalone cell pays 240 selection plus all candidate draws through its terminal look, including repeats and unaccepted draws. Standalone policy sums four cells. Shared sequential union pays selection once per group plus the largest terminal look among seven policies. Fixed shared union pays four*(240+960). Actual joint research acquisition shares selection and the full fixed stream, paying 4800 labels per replicate, not the sum of standalone costs. Oracle census and pilot labels are separate research overhead; retained historical fit labels are not current labels.

motivation.scope: Sequential feasibility motivation only; the proof here is a finite union bound.

methods.numerical_convention: exact integer binomial CDF at risk1/20; no float tolerance; invalid bound output aborts all arms
methods.proof_obligations: At fixed p, couple Bernoulli sums by adding one independent trial. P(Bin(n+1,p)<=e)<=P(Bin(n,p)<=e), while increasing e increases this CDF. Inverting the CDF gives an upper bound decreasing in n and increasing in e. At future draw L after t, every attainable state satisfies n_future<=n+L-t and e_future>=e. Thus (n+L-t,e) minimizes the exact upper bound. Rejecting every optimistic future test proves every attainable future test fails. An already issued certificate is permanent. Until safe refusal, both sequential arms visit identical prefixes; after it neither can pass. Their decisions are therefore equal on every path. Fixed final certificates remain included. Statistical error separately uses the unchanged finite family union bound; stationary iid group draws independent of selection remain required. No theorem from the motivating sequential feasibility papers is imported.
methods.refusal_rule: all remaining optimistic tests fail; every additional draw accepted with zero new errors
methods.selection_rule: Group cutoffs maximize accepted selection draws at empirical risk<=.05; ties higher cutoff. Both protocols share the same rule; empty refuses after full budget.
methods.shared_cost: 240 selection requests per group plus maximum policy stop; request ordinals shared once, replacement repeats paid

protocol.shared_benefit: primary lower99>0; zero decision or inclusion violations; valid controls; every served census risk<=.05

target_model: seven frozen numerical policies; no current model load or training

theoretical_family_error.scope: per replicate conditional on frozen selection
